conflicts.fact: Which lesson establishes the cohesion-tension / transpiration pull mechanism, and what drives water up the xylem
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 says the full mechanism (cohesion-tension, transpiration pull) will be established in Lesson 7, and its DQB note says the question about what drives water all the way up is Lesson 3's topic. Lesson 3 says root pressure is the push that explains why the dye rose and defers the remaining question to Lesson 4. Lesson 4 is about phloem and defers transpiration to Lesson 5. Lesson 7 says transpiration pull is the primary force. Lesson 3 gives root pressure as the explanation for the dye moving up, which conflicts with Lesson 7.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson contained the polythene-bag observation and the stomata notes
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 refers to the polythene-bag observation 'from Lesson 3' and Lesson 5 tells learners to check their stomata notes 'from Lesson 3', but the bag was observed in Lesson 1 (Lesson 6 correctly says Lesson 1) and Lesson 3 covers root absorption, not stomata.

conflicts.fact: Which lessons produced the transpiration (potometer) data
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 says the data table from Lessons 4–5 on stomata count, wind, temperature and humidity came from potometer experiments, but the experiments were set up in Lesson 5 and analysed in Lesson 6. Lesson 4 is about phloem, and temperature was not a tested variable (light was).

conflicts.fact: Location and appearance of the red-stained tissue in the maize stem
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says red appears in dot-shaped regions or rings. Lesson 2 describes scattered vascular bundles and also says xylem is arranged in rings or bundles. Lesson 4 says the colourless outer tissue of the bundle is phloem and the stained rings are xylem. Lesson 4 teaches 'phloem on outer edge', whereas Lessons 1 and 2 describe the outer green tissue and pith as simply white.

conflicts.fact: Direction of phloem transport and the effect of girdling
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 says translocation goes from source to sink, with swelling above the girdle. Lesson 8 says sugars travel 'downward and upward', and that girdling kills the plant 'above the cut', whereas Lesson 4 says trees die eventually, because roots starve below the cut.

conflicts.fact: Plant used in the bag set-up
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 calls it a bean or sweet potato cutting. Lesson 8 refers to a leafy cutting from a succulent plant. Sweet potato and bean are not succulents. Lesson 5 says sweet potato or bean.
